steps.title: Three questions, one tool
steps.body:
The maximum / minimum tool gives a turning point as a pair \((x,\,y)\). Read the question to see which part it wants:
•  “the maximum point” or “the coordinates of the maximum”: both, \((0.465,\,3.88)\)
•  “the maximum value” or “the greatest value of \(f\)”: \(y\) only, \(3.88\)
•  “the value of \(x\) at which \(f\) is greatest”: \(x\) only, \(0.465\)

steps.title: “Find the value of \(x\) for which \(f\) is least.” The answer is
steps.ok: ✓ Right. “The value of \(x\)” means the \(x\)-coordinate only.
bads: ✗ \(-3.06\) is the least value of \(f\); the question asks where it happens: \(x=2.87\).
✗ The pair is the minimum point; the question asks for \(x\) only: \(2.87\).

steps.title: On a domain, check the endpoints

nspire.body:
The tool finds turning points. The greatest or least value on a domain can also be at an end of the domain, where there is no turning point:
•  find the turning points inside the domain with the tool
•  find the value of \(f\) at each endpoint
•  the greatest (or least) of all of these is the answer

On \(-1\le x\le4\): the local minimum is \(-3.06\), but \(f(-1)=-7\) is lower, so the least value is \(-7\). Endpoint values on the Nspire: f1(4) on a Calculator page, or Graph Trace and type the x.

steps.title: What the examiner wants to see
steps.body:
Name the point and say where it came from:
•  “maximum at \((0.465,\,3.88)\) (from GDC)”, then the part the question asked for
•  on a domain: the endpoint values as well, so the comparison is visible

Two habits that lose marks:
•  giving \(x\) when the question wants the value, or the other way round
•  “by GDC” with no coordinates written down

steps.title: Optimisation: the model does the work
steps.body:
When a question gives a model (profit, area, volume, cost), the best value is a turning point:
•  graph the model with the domain from the story (\(x\ge0\), a length less than the sheet, …)
•  maximum or minimum tool: \(x\) is “how many / what size”, \(y\) is “the best value”
•  units, and sensible rounding: \(40\) items, \(\$650\); not \(40.0000\)

steps.title: Minimums, and two-stage answers
steps.body:
The same tool, the other way up:
•  cost, time, distance, surface area: usually a minimum
•  if the model has a fraction (\(2000/x\)) the graph shoots up near \(x=0\): set Ymax high enough to see the trough
•  two-stage questions: find \(x\) from the tool, then substitute it back to get the other quantity (the dimensions, the height, the cost)
